summary: Presence counts unique users across all their socket references; repeat joins no longer trigger duplicate presence updates.
Room events validate payloads and require the established connection identity and joined room; agent subscription checks the existing demo session role.
Message insertion, room activity and sender receipt commit together before broadcast or successful acknowledgement.
Read-through and history ordering distinguish messages sharing a timestamp.
Client subscriptions use stable room IDs and reconnect state; user switching disconnects old identity, and read/send operations wait for room join completion.
Nine detailed learning documents plus an updated architecture guide teach the actual code, real connection tests, failure cases, examples and mid-level extensions.

checks.command: npm test -- --test-reporter=tap; npm run build --prefix client
checks.environment: Node 22.16.0; npm 10.9.2; locked installs; real Socket.IO clients/server over websocket transport and SQLite memory database

limits: No live browser or component interaction tests; React changes were source-reviewed and built.
REST endpoints, production entrypoint, physical uploads and persistent-file restart were not verified.
Demo identity is caller-controlled; private-room and REST authorization remain unimplemented.
Attachment metadata validation does not prove file ownership, existence or safety.
No message idempotency key, complete timestamp-tie pagination cursor, or cross-process presence coordination.
